# Bedrock
Bedrock is a lightweight Bun personal cloud hosting small projects called pebbles.
Read AGENTS.md for the API and ARCHITECTURE.md in the repository for the contract.
Package entry points: bedrock (config + Drizzle), bedrock/server (startPebble), bedrock/daemon (startDaemon).
CLI: bedrock init <name>, bedrock dev, bedrock db generate|plan|migrate.
All commands accept --json. No build step; Bun runs TypeScript source.
Phase 1 includes config, SQLite migrations/tracking, HTTP functions, static/HTML web, and CLI.
Phase 2 includes the daemon, host proxy (HTTP + WebSockets), subprocess supervision, deploy/rollback, tokens, and rotated logs.
CLI: setup, daemon, deploy [dir], ls, logs <name> [-f], start|stop|restart <name>, rollback <name>, rm <name> --yes, token create.
Daemon API requires Bearer tokens; flags --url/--token override env BEDROCK_URL/BEDROCK_TOKEN, then local BEDROCK_HOME defaults.
Phase 3 includes Google OAuth/PKCE, hashed sliding sessions, signed identity, access policies and local dev login.
Dev serves http://<name>.localhost:<port>; protected pages redirect to host-local /_bedrock/dev-login.
Production Google redirect URI: https://auth.<domain>/callback; setup accepts --google-client-id and --google-client-secret.
Session cookies never reach pebble code. The daemon keeps a per-boot master in memory and derives each child identity secret with HMAC-SHA256(master, "identity:" + pebbleName). Writes/WebSocket upgrades require the pebble's own Origin.
Sync, bedrock/client and bedrock/react are implemented: client.user(), loginUrl(), logout(), useUser().
Plugin execution belongs to a later phase.
Phase 4 includes WebSocket sync, the typed browser client, and React hooks. Phase 5 includes filesystem storage, streamed/chunked uploads, access policies, safe downloads, and byte ranges.
Declare const attachments = bucket("attachments", { maxSize: "50mb", access: "owner", accept: ["image/*"] }); register storage: [attachments].
Bucket names: [a-z0-9_-]{1,32}, unique per pebble. bucket() and definePebble() validate with hints.
query(fn) / query(schema, fn) and mutation(fn) / mutation(schema, fn) are the only function signatures.
ctx.storage.put(attachments, blobOrStream, { name, mime? }), get(attachments, id), delete(attachments, id), list(attachments, { ownerId?, limit?, cursor? }).
put returns metadata; get returns a Blob; list returns metadata. Unregistered bucket objects throw UNKNOWN_BUCKET with a repair hint.
Before linking attachments, await storage.get(attachments, attachmentId) with access: "owner" to verify ownership; see examples/notes.
createClient<typeof pebble>() from bedrock/client infers upload/fileUrl/deleteFile bucket names from the storage array. Clients accept names, not server bucket objects.
useUpload<typeof pebble>("attachments") from bedrock/react exposes upload, progress, isUploading, error. The SDK transparently chunks files above 90 MiB.

Phase 6: tunnel, service, doctor, remote creator login, and deploy token management.
CLI: tunnel setup --account-id <id> --zone-id <id> [--api-token <token>], tunnel status, tunnel teardown --yes.
Cloudflare API token comes from flag/env CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN/hidden prompt; never persisted. Permissions: Cloudflare Tunnel: Edit and DNS: Edit.
Setup reconciles bedrock-<hostname>, wildcard ingress and proxied CNAME. Public domain/fixed port required; restart daemon after setup.
Only the tunnel run token is persisted (BEDROCK_HOME/tunnel-token, 0600); metadata in config.json. cloudflared uses TUNNEL_TOKEN env, never argv.
cloudflared restarts with capped backoff; local serving survives failures. logs/cloudflared.log rotates and redacts the token.
CLI: service install|uninstall|status [--dry-run]. Dry-run prints the plist/unit, writes nothing, invokes no service manager.
macOS LaunchAgent: ~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.bedrock.daemon.plist (at user login). Linux systemd user: ~/.config/systemd/user/bedrock.service; loginctl enable-linger "$USER" for startup without login.
CLI: doctor [--json]. JSON is an array of pass/warn/fail checks with hints; exit 1 on any fail. API verification skips without token; DoH skips offline.
CLI: login --url https://bedrock.<domain>, logout, token create|ls|revoke <id>. Login requires browser creator session and explicit single-use confirmation; random loopback callback state is checked.
Remote credentials: ~/.config/bedrock/credentials.json (XDG_CONFIG_HOME supported), {url, token}, 0600. Used when local daemon unavailable; --url/--token then env take precedence.
Tokens never follow redirects. Logout revokes remotely before deleting local credentials and retains them on network failure.
Deploy tokens are hashed in SQLite; ls returns IDs/timestamps, revoke invalidates immediately. All creator deploy tokens have full daemon management access.
API additions: GET /api/status, GET /api/tokens, DELETE /api/tokens/<id>, DELETE /api/tokens/current (Bearer required).
Repeat login verifies/reuses valid credentials; logout before switching servers.
